evidence.ac_hash_recipe: sha256 over JSON.stringify of the array of the six fenced bodies (ac1..ac6 order), each body the full `bash -c '...'` one-liner as it sits between the ```bash fences in docs/issues/groom/t65.md, CR-stripped and trimmed - the t58/t62/t63/t64 recipe. DIALECT MATTERS: JSON.stringify means COMPACT separators (no space after the comma) and plain ASCII escaping; a Python json.dumps default adds ', ' and yields a different digest (sha256:ba7906b2... vs the recorded sha256:3103ef0e...). The builders now emit separators=(',',':') and assert the fence bodies are ASCII so the two dialects cannot diverge, and the value is RECOMPUTED independently from the committed mirror blob after commit (see evidence.post_commit_recompute) rather than trusted from the generator.

design_decisions.module_contract: constants DEMO_EMAIL/DEMO_PASSWORD/DEMO_USERNAME, SPAN_DAYS=90, RNG_SEED; wipe_demo_data(bind) and seed_demo_data(bind) are Core-only and NEVER commit; main() owns the engine and the transaction; the anchor is date.today() overridable by SEED_DEMO_ANCHOR=YYYY-MM-DD; generation is a pure function of day offset 0..89 driven by random.Random(RNG_SEED); main() honours the effective DATABASE_URL from app settings.
design_decisions.why_anchor_override_exists: ac6 must compare two anchors in ONE run. Without an override the determinism leg could only be observed once per day, so the gate would be unverifiable rather than wrong.
design_decisions.why_core_only: the merged seed.py precedent (seed_system_categories(bind) -> int, never commits) and it lets the builder compose wipe+seed inside one transaction owned by main(), which is what makes the re-run atomic - ac4's three-run equality depends on it.
design_decisions.wipe_scope: demo expenses, budgets and audit rows plus the demo user row. Audit rows are deleted explicitly because audit_logs.user_id has no ON DELETE CASCADE (measured in the merged model). The wipe must NEVER delete the shared system categories (user_id NULL) - ac5 fences that with a ==10 assertion, because deleting them would break every other account while leaving the demo account looking correct.
design_decisions.npm_line: "seed:demo": "cd backend && uv run python -m app.scripts.seed_demo" - cd-then-run rather than a --cwd flag so the seed resolves the same settings, .env lookup and relative SQLite path the dev server uses. ac1 matches the two semantic fragments and rejects anything else.
design_decisions.probe_databases: every fence creates its own SQLite file under the gitignored build/ directory, migrates it with the DATABASE_URL override, and deletes it at the end. No fence ever points the seed at backend/dev.db; ac1 additionally asserts the dev.db digest is unchanged across the npm invocation.
design_decisions.test_file_4_trigger: backend/tests/integration/test_seed_demo_api.py is permitted ONLY if the login/dashboard assertions cannot be proven inside the unit module; the trigger is that TestClient + dependency_overrides[get_db] is the merged t8/t11 integration pattern. If file 4 is not created, ac2's two node IDs move to the unit module - the fences pin node IDs, not directories.
design_decisions.w5_limits: max_files=4 (used as the ceiling, with file 4 conditional and its trigger stated in the card), max_acs=6 (exactly 6 used), max_diff_lines=300 warn-only - a 90-day generator plus two test modules can legitimately exceed 300 lines, so the cap stays advisory and is stated as such in the DoD rather than quietly ignored.
design_decisions.no_req_id: operator-directed capability, no requirement-id anchor; authority is the README live-demo requirement plus the operator directive of 2026-10-15. The card is generator-inert: 0 full-form ids (measured), and ac6 builds its synthetic control id from fragments at runtime so the inertness grep is provably non-vacuous.

The operator repair path is `npm run setup:local`, which builds a win32 venv.
environment_facts.node_tools: node v18.19.1; tsx and the platform CLI must run through cmd.exe (node_modules esbuild is win32-native: `node node_modules\tsx\dist\cli.mjs ...`), while uv/python run under WSL. Both halves were used in this groom.
environment_facts.fence_form: one `bash -c '...'` line, exactly two single quotes (the delimiters), no inner single quote, no heredoc, no backtick, CRLF-tolerant via tr -d, all under the 8191-byte Windows CreateProcess ceiling. Inline python probes are staged by decoding a base64 payload to /tmp and running it under uv run: a single-quoted one-liner cannot carry embedded newlines, and printf with escaped double quotes does not interpret them, so the base64 channel is the only form that satisfies both constraints. This is the single most likely way this card misleads a builder: the fences look opaque because their probes are encoded, and the sources live at scratch/t65/fences/*.py.

ac1 is the only fence that invokes the npm script, and it does so with DATABASE_URL pointed at a probe database. If the builder's main() ignores the effective DATABASE_URL, ac1 goes RED with 'the run wrote no database at the DATABASE_URL override path' rather than silently writing the operator's dev.db.

ac4's equality is a wipe+rebuild proof, not a no-op proof: three runs must produce the SAME snapshot while a one-row deletion moves the digest. An implementation that appends instead of wiping shows a growing count; one that no-ops shows zero duplicates but a stale dataset - the digest equality catches both.
ac6 re-runs the full backend suite (~100 s at base) plus two migrations and two seeds; the six fences together measured roughly 8-10 minutes on this box with a warm uv cache.
